raw.Funder_Names: Research Fund of Guizhou Provincial Health Commission; Science and Technology Joint Funds of Zunyi Science and Technology Bureau & The First People's Hospital of Zunyi
raw.Population_Description: 297 consecutive Neuro-ICU patients discharged from a grade-A tertiary hospital in Guizhou province, China (Jan 2018-Apr 2020); 131 infected with MDRO (infection rate 44.11%).
raw.Top_Predictive_Features: Multivariable (binary logistic regression) independent risk factors: antibiotics (OR 8.064 - the most important factor), artery blood pressure monitoring (OR 7.479), tracheal intubation (OR 6.140), pneumonia (OR 5.755), fever (OR 5.209), albumin (OR 0.920, protective/higher level lower risk). Importance method: adjusted odds ratios from multiple logistic regression (Table 2).
raw.Provider_Facing_Applications: Screening / risk stratification
raw.All_Models_Evaluated: Binary logistic regression risk prediction model (five clinical predictors + albumin); reported AUC 0.887 (95% CI 0.849-0.925), sensitivity 86.3%, specificity 78.9%, Hosmer-Lemeshow P = 0.831, Youden index 0.652, cutoff 0.476. No comparator models were evaluated.
raw.Best_Performing_Model: Binary logistic regression risk prediction model (the only model developed and evaluated; decision metric = AUC 0.887 on the 297-patient Neuro-ICU cohort)
raw.Accuracy_Population_Set: Neuro-ICU patients, n = 297 (model construction cohort)
raw.Sensitivity_Population_Set: Neuro-ICU patients, n = 297 (model construction cohort)
raw.Specificity_Population_Set: Neuro-ICU patients, n = 297 (model construction cohort)
raw.AUROC_Population_Set: Neuro-ICU patients, n = 297 (model construction cohort)
raw.Clinical_Maturity_Justification: Single-centre retrospective development of a logistic risk model evaluated only by apparent ROC performance on the same 297 patients; the authors state there was no further verification of the prediction model and no assessment of its impact on actual MDRO incidence.
raw.Reported_Limitations: Single-centre retrospective design, data from one hospital in one province that cannot represent the region or country (possible bias); small sample (small Neuro-ICU population, only two years of data); no further validation of the prediction model and no investigation of its impact on actual MDRO infection incidence.
raw.Ethical_Governance_Risks: Ethics committee approval obtained (2017-215); patient information anonymised and deidentified before analysis so informed consent was waived; research performed per the Declaration of Helsinki. No AI-specific governance or risk discussion.

raw.Conflicts_of_Interest: The authors declare no competing interests.

raw.Exclusion_Criteria: Patients with incomplete data or an MDRO infection that has occurred.
raw.Data_Types_Used: Clinical / EHR variables; Demographic variables; Prescription / dispensing data
raw.Dataset_Size: 297 patients, 131 MDRO-infected (infection rate 44.11%)
raw.Geographic_Representativeness: Authors state the single tertiary hospital in one province cannot represent the actual situation in the region or the whole country; patients lost to transfer or death meant the exact infection rate could not be calculated.
raw.Specimen_Type_Detail: sputum, blood, cerebrospinal fluid, and midstream urine
raw.Primary_AMR_Outcome: MDRO (multi-drug-resistant organism) infection in Neuro-ICU patients
raw.Pathogens: Acinetobacter baumannii; Klebsiella pneumoniae; Pseudomonas pyocyaneum; Methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus; Escherichia coli
raw.Drug_Classes: sulfonamides, quinolones and β-lactam antibiotics
raw.AMR_Outcome_Definition: MDRO defined per the 2010 international standardized definition of MDROs jointly proposed by the United States and other countries; patients grouped by whether they were infected or colonized with MDRO, judged from aseptically collected sputum, blood, cerebrospinal fluid and midstream urine samples.
raw.AI_Purpose: Develop and validate a risk prediction model for MDRO infection in Neuro-ICU patients from independent risk factors, to evaluate risk and provide reference for preventive treatment and nursing intervention.
raw.Num_Models_Compared: 1 (a single binary logistic regression model; no comparator models developed or benchmarked)
raw.Feature_Engineering: Data collection items designed from literature/expert discussion: general demographic information (gender, age), treatment circumstances (invasive operation, level of consciousness), laboratory indicators and the patient's own physical conditions; no engineered transformations described.
raw.Feature_Selection_Method: Univariate analysis followed by multivariate (binary logistic regression) screening of risk factors
raw.Software_Libraries: SPSS 20.0
raw.Other_Metrics: Youden index 0.652; optimal cutoff value 0.476
raw.Clinical_Insights: Antibiotic use was the most important predictor (OR 8.064); invasive artery blood pressure monitoring and tracheal intubation destroy physiological integrity and local immune function; lower serum albumin associated with higher infection risk; fever and pneumonia also predictors; GCS severity score did not predict MDRO.
raw.Data_Repository: Supplementary material of the online article (Springer Nature, DOI 10.1038/s41598-023-42522-2)
raw.Generalisability_Details: Authors note data from one tertiary hospital in one province cannot represent the region or the whole country, that the cohort excludes patients transferred out or who died, and that the exact infection rate could not be calculated.
raw.Maturity_Evidence: Development and apparent-performance evaluation on the same 297-patient cohort (ROC AUC 0.887); the authors state there was no further verification of the prediction model and no assessment of its impact on actual MDRO incidence - level 1.

raw.End_User_Described: physicians, pharmacists, and nurses
raw.Clinical_Workflow_Details: Authors propose multidisciplinary coordination - clinicians and pharmacists co-managing therapeutic medication, routine MDR screening after ICU admission, and nurses active in day-to-day MDRO prevention and management.
raw.Future_Directions: Reinforce multidisciplinary coordination so physicians, pharmacists and nurses play a more active role; make MDR screening a routine part of post-admission care; pharmacists to guide standardised medication regimens; nurses to lead day-to-day MDRO prevention.
raw.Top_Features_Importance_Method: Adjusted odds ratios (OR, 95% CI) from the multiple logistic regression model; the paper ranks antibiotics as the most important factor
raw.Novel_Predictors_Details: The authors contrast their findings with the past: their model identified artery blood pressure monitoring and tracheal intubation, whereas previous work reported urinary tubes and feeding tubes as the main indwelling instruments associated with MDRO infection.
raw.Limitation_Categories: Single-centre retrospective design / non-representative setting; small sample size; no validation of the model and no assessment of its clinical impact.
raw.Data_Quality_Concerns: Patients transferred to other hospitals or who died during ICU stay were excluded from the analysis, so the exact MDRO infection rate could not be calculated.

studies.title: Direct antimicrobial resistance prediction from clinical MALDI-TOF mass spectra using machine learning
studies.sample_size: 303,195 mass spectra and 768,300 antimicrobial resistance labels from more than 300,000 clinical isolates (DRIAMS-A, the main analysis dataset: 145,341 mass spectra); retrospective clinical case study: 416 cases reviewed of which 63 included
studies.ai_purpose: To predict antimicrobial resistance directly from clinical MALDI-TOF mass spectra of isolates using calibrated machine-learning classifiers (LightGBM, MLP, logistic regression), in order to accelerate resistance determination, support antibiotic treatment optimisation and promote antibiotic stewardship.
studies.pathogens_reported: Staphylococcus aureus, Escherichia coli and Klebsiella pneumoniae (focused analysis, all WHO priority pathogens); the full DRIAMS dataset represents 803 different species of bacterial and fungal pathogens
studies.resistance_type: Binary R/S for a single drug; ESBL; MRSA
studies.best_model: LightGBM - highest AUROC on the primary dataset DRIAMS-A: 0.80 for oxacillin resistance in S. aureus (LightGBM and MLP were jointly named the best-performing classifiers by AUROC; MLP was best for K. pneumoniae ceftriaxone at 0.74)

raw.Title: Direct antimicrobial resistance prediction from clinical MALDI-TOF mass spectra using machine learning
raw.AI_Application_Type: AI Predictive and Prognostic Models; AI Laboratory Specimen Interpretation
raw.Funder_Names: Alfried Krupp von Bohlen und Halbach-Stiftung (Alfried Krupp Prize for Young University Teachers); the two Cantons of Basel through a D-BSSE-Uni-Basel Personalised Medicine grant from ETH Zurich (PMB-03-17); Swiss National Science Foundation Doc.Mobility fellowship (P1BSP3-184342)
raw.Population_Description: MALDI-TOF mass spectra of routinely acquired clinical bacterial and fungal isolates from four Swiss diagnostic laboratories (2016-2018), linked to laboratory-confirmed antimicrobial resistance profiles; the retrospective clinical case study reviews 63 patients with invasive infections caused by E. coli, K. pneumoniae or S. aureus
raw.Data_Source_Other: MALDI-TOF mass spectra files from clinical Bruker Microflex Biotyper systems
raw.Top_Predictive_Features: Highest-ranked binned m/z features by mean |SHAP value| (30 top bins per scenario, Fig. 5). S. aureus (oxacillin, LightGBM): top bins such as 4,511-4,514 Da, 4,277-4,280 Da, 5,666-5,669 Da; for the top four m/z bins a peak indicates the resistant/intermediate class. E. coli (ceftriaxone, LightGBM): bins such as 2,288-2,291 Da, 2,336-2,339 Da, 7,715-7,718 Da; absence of a peak can also contribute. K. pneumoniae (ceftriaxone, MLP): bins such as 9,761-9,764 Da, 6,878-6,881 Da, 11,783-11,786 Da. Named contributing peaks: 3,007 Da (Delta-toxin), 3,891 Da (uncharacterized protein SA2420.1), 4,511 Da (uncharacterized protein SAR1012); a peak at 2,415 m/z (bin 2,414-2,417, ranked 83rd of 6,000) previously identified as MRSA-specific (PSM-mec); ST131-characteristic peaks 8,448, 8,496 and 11,783 m/z.
raw.Provider_Facing_Applications: Resistance prediction (phenotype from genotype or spectra); Treatment / prescribing guidance
raw.All_Models_Evaluated: Logistic regression, LightGBM (gradient-boosted decision trees) and MLP (multilayer perceptron). DRIAMS-A, mean over 10 shuffled stratified train-test splits: S. aureus oxacillin AUROC 0.80 / AUPRC 0.49 (LightGBM); E. coli ceftriaxone AUROC 0.74 / AUPRC 0.30 (LightGBM); K. pneumoniae ceftriaxone AUROC 0.74 / AUPRC 0.33 (MLP). Other DRIAMS-A scenarios (Fig. 2): E. coli ciprofloxacin AUROC 0.68, cefepime 0.76, meropenem 0.55, tobramycin 0.74; K. pneumoniae ciprofloxacin 0.76, cefepime 0.73, piperacillin-tazobactam 0.60, tobramycin 0.64; S. aureus ciprofloxacin 0.72, fusidic acid 0.65. Across the 42 antibiotics studied with all-species logistic regression, 31 reached AUROC > 0.80.
raw.Best_Performing_Model: LightGBM - highest AUROC on the primary dataset DRIAMS-A: 0.80 for oxacillin resistance in S. aureus (LightGBM and MLP were jointly named the best-performing classifiers by AUROC; MLP was best for K. pneumoniae ceftriaxone at 0.74)
raw.AUROC_Population_Set: DRIAMS-A test set, S. aureus oxacillin-resistance scenario (LightGBM); mean of 10 different shuffled stratified train-test splits
raw.Clinical_Maturity_Justification: Algorithm developed and internally validated on DRIAMS-A (fivefold cross-validation for hyperparameters, 80/20 stratified train-test splits) and then applied across sites, i.e. trained at one site and tested on the external sites DRIAMS-B, -C and -D. No prospective evaluation and no clinical deployment is reported, so the highest level supported is external validation.
raw.Reported_Limitations: Performance of classifiers trained at one site is not generalizable to spectra measured at other sites (phylogenetic differences, differing resistance prevalence/class ratios, technical batch effects); predictive power decreases with increasing temporal distance between training and prediction data; many resistance-causing proteins are outside the effective mass range of MALDI-TOF MS; the four sites are all in a low-endemic area for ESBL-producing and MRSA bacteria; the clinical case study is retrospective and prospective multicentre evaluation is still needed.
raw.Unintended_Consequences_Harms: In one of the 63 clinical cases a false resistance prediction would have led to an unnecessary escalation to a broader-spectrum antibiotic; in three cases the algorithm predicted susceptibility when phenotypic testing showed resistance, but this did not lead to less effective treatment.
raw.Equity_Fairness_Concerns: Not discussed - no equity or fairness analysis is reported; the dataset is de-identified mass spectra with resistance labels and no demographic variables.
raw.Ethical_Governance_Risks: The study was evaluated by the local ethics committee (IEC 2019-00729; EKNZ numbers IEC 2019-00729, 2019-01860 and 2019-00748) and all data used for the machine learning analysis were de-identified prior to analysis.
raw.Reviewer_Notes: Judgement calls recorded: (1) First_Author_Year is 2022 (published online 10 January 2022, Nature Medicine vol. 28, January 2022) while the record/DOI year label in the batch is 2023. (2) Study_Setting coded 'Mixed': spectra come from diagnostic laboratories serving hospitals and private practices, and the clinical case study is set in a tertiary hospital. (3) Sensitivity/Specificity/Precision coded 'No' because only ROC/precision-recall curves and AUROC/AUPRC values are reported - no numeric sensitivity, specificity or PPV value is given for the best model. (4) Calibration coded 'No': the paper describes 'calibrated classifiers' but reports no calibration method or metric. (5) AUPRC values are reported with a positive class ratio (10.0% in the text vs 10.6% in Fig. 2c for S. aureus oxacillin).
raw.Sample_Size: 303,195 mass spectra and 768,300 antimicrobial resistance labels from more than 300,000 clinical isolates (DRIAMS-A, the main analysis dataset: 145,341 mass spectra); retrospective clinical case study: 416 cases reviewed of which 63 included
raw.Conflicts_of_Interest: The authors declare no competing interests.
raw.Inclusion_Criteria: All MALDI-TOF mass spectra measured in the given time frames at the four participating laboratories are included; spectra are matched to their laboratory-confirmed antimicrobial resistance profiles via a unique sample ID-genus (or sample ID-species) identifier; samples with a missing resistance profile are removed per antibiotic.
raw.Exclusion_Criteria: Empty and calibration spectra excluded; samples collected for the hospital hygiene department excluded from DRIAMS-A; spectra/samples without a unique sample ID-genus pair omitted; spectra that could not be matched to a laboratory result entry ignored; spectra without an antimicrobial resistance profile not used for supervised learning.
raw.Data_Types_Used: MALDI-TOF mass spectra; AST phenotypic results
raw.Data_Source_Name: DRIAMS (Database of Resistance Information on Antimicrobials and MALDI-TOF Mass Spectra)
raw.Dataset_Size: 303,195 mass spectra and 768,300 antimicrobial resistance labels (803 species); DRIAMS-A 145,341 spectra; DRIAMS-B 186,098 spectra; DRIAMS-C 12,110 spectra; DRIAMS-D 80,796 spectra
raw.Missing_Data_Method: Complete-case removal - all samples with a missing antimicrobial resistance profile were removed for each antibiotic before modelling
raw.Geographic_Representativeness: Four Swiss diagnostic laboratories: University Hospital Basel (DRIAMS-A, main analysis, patients mainly from Basel and surroundings), Canton Hospital Basel-Land (DRIAMS-B), Canton Hospital Aarau (DRIAMS-C, patients from Canton Aargau) and Viollier, a service provider for medical practices and hospitals all over Switzerland (DRIAMS-D). All sites are in a low-endemic area for ESBL-producing and MRSA bacteria.
raw.Specimen_Type_Detail: clinical isolates from routine diagnostic samples; retrospective case study: positive cultures of E. coli, K. pneumoniae or S. aureus from blood culture or deep tissue samples
raw.Primary_AMR_Outcome: Binary antimicrobial resistance prediction per species-antibiotic pair (positive class = intermediate or resistant, negative class = susceptible), evaluated mainly for oxacillin resistance in S. aureus and ceftriaxone resistance in E. coli and K. pneumoniae on DRIAMS-A
raw.Pathogens: Staphylococcus aureus, Escherichia coli and Klebsiella pneumoniae (focused analysis, all WHO priority pathogens); the full DRIAMS dataset represents 803 different species of bacterial and fungal pathogens
raw.Num_Pathogens: 3 focused species (S. aureus, E. coli, K. pneumoniae); 803 species overall in DRIAMS
raw.Drug_Classes: Beta-lactams (oxacillin, ceftriaxone, cefepime, meropenem, piperacillin-tazobactam); fluoroquinolones (ciprofloxacin); aminoglycosides (tobramycin); fusidane (fusidic acid)
raw.Specific_Antibiotics: Oxacillin, ceftriaxone, ciprofloxacin, cefepime, meropenem, tobramycin, piperacillin-tazobactam, fusidic acid; DRIAMS-A contains resistance labels for 71 different antimicrobial drugs and 42 antibiotics were analysed in the all-species comparison
raw.Resistance_Phenotype_Reported: Binary R/S for a single drug; ESBL; MRSA
raw.AMR_Outcome_Definition: Resistant (R) and intermediate (I) samples labelled as class 1 and susceptible (S) samples as class 0; resistance categories were recorded as susceptible, intermediate or resistant in the laboratory reports and binarized as susceptible versus intermediate or resistant.
raw.AI_Purpose: To predict antimicrobial resistance directly from clinical MALDI-TOF mass spectra of isolates using calibrated machine-learning classifiers (LightGBM, MLP, logistic regression), in order to accelerate resistance determination, support antibiotic treatment optimisation and promote antibiotic stewardship.
raw.Feature_Engineering: Spectra preprocessed in R with MaldiQuant v1.19: (1) square-root variance stabilisation, (2) Savitzky-Golay smoothing with half-window-size 10, (3) baseline removal with 20 iterations of the SNIP algorithm, (4) total ion current intensity calibration, (5) trimming to 2,000-20,000 Da; then binned into fixed bins of 3 Da giving a 6,000-dimensional feature vector per spectrum.
raw.Feature_Selection_Method: None - no feature selection was applied; classifiers utilise the entire range of all 6,000 feature bins
raw.Class_Imbalance_Method: Training data oversampled to match the class ratio of the test data in the temporal validation; AUROC (class-ratio invariant) used as the main metric and AUPRC reported because 20 of 42 antibiotics have a resistant/intermediate class ratio <20% or >80%
raw.Hyperparameter_Method: Fivefold cross-validation on the training data (threefold fallback when too few samples), optimising AUROC on the training dataset only; grid includes L1/L2/no penalty, standardisation choice and regularisation parameters C in {1e-3 ... 1e3}
raw.Software_Libraries: lightgbm; scikit-learn; shap; pandas/numpy; MaldiQuant v1.19 (R) for spectra preprocessing
raw.Other_Metrics: AUPRC reported alongside AUROC; sensitivity versus specificity curves; AUPRC baseline given by the positive class ratio (e.g. 10.0% for S. aureus oxacillin, 8.2% for K. pneumoniae ceftriaxone); SHAP values and model feature importances; performance expressed as mean +/- standard deviation over repetitions.
raw.Baseline_Method: Classifiers trained on species-identity information only (logistic regression, Extended Data Fig. 2) compared with mass-spectra-based classifiers; random binary classifier, whose AUPRC equals the positive class ratio
raw.Baseline_Performance: For 31 of 42 studied antibiotics an AUROC above 0.80 was reached with mass spectra, and for 22 antibiotics mass-spectra models significantly improved on species-information-only prediction; AUPRC of a random binary classifier equals the positive class ratio (10.0% for S. aureus oxacillin).
raw.Internal_Validation: Fivefold cross-validation on the training data (threefold fallback) for hyperparameter selection; reported metrics are means over 10 different shuffled stratified train-test splits (80% train / 20% test, stratified by antimicrobial class and patient case).
raw.Train_Test_Split: 80% training and 20% test, stratified by both antimicrobial class and patient case number
raw.External_Validation_Description: Trained on one site and tested on other collection sites among DRIAMS-A-D; adding the large DRIAMS-A dataset to the training data improved prediction for the external validation sites DRIAMS-B (E. coli and K. pneumoniae ceftriaxone) and DRIAMS-C, while DRIAMS-D performed best with site-specific training only.
raw.Overfitting_Method: Grouped train-test splitting at patient-case level so that measurements of the same infection cannot leak between training and testing, plus stratification by class and species; performance also reported as mean over 10 randomised splits.
raw.Clinical_Insights: The most impactful feature bins have m/z below 10,000 Da (79 of 90 bins in Fig. 5), consistent with the mass range of reproducibly detected proteins; a peak at 2,415 m/z (PSM-mec, near mecA) previously identified as MRSA-specific is the 83rd highest-ranked bin; ST131-characteristic peaks (8,448, 8,496, 11,783 m/z) are highly ranked by the E. coli ceftriaxone classifier; named contributing peaks are 3,007 Da (Delta-toxin), 3,891 Da (SA2420.1) and 4,511 Da (SAR1012), supporting that the classifiers detect resistance-associated proteome changes rather than confounding noise.
raw.Generalisability_Details: Performance achieved at one site is not generalizable to spectra measured at other sites or at later timepoints; a clinically applied classifier should be retrained regularly with recent data from its deployment site and may require regular re-certification; all contributing sites are in a low-endemic area, so behaviour in high-burden settings is unknown.
raw.Maturity_Evidence: External validation: classifiers trained on one DRIAMS site were tested on the other sites (DRIAMS-B, -C, -D); site-specific training outperformed across-site validation and DRIAMS-A was the most transferable training dataset. Internal validation (fivefold cross-validation, 10 shuffled train-test splits) preceded this. No prospective or deployed evaluation.
raw.Integration_Point: Infectious diseases consultation after MALDI-TOF species identification and before phenotypic resistance results, to adjust empiric antibiotic therapy
raw.End_User_Described: infectious diseases specialist / clinician, and clinical microbiology laboratories already using MALDI-TOF MS for species identification
raw.Clinical_Workflow_Details: Current standard of care: empiric regimen, species identification by MALDI-TOF MS, then adjustment based on phenotypic resistance testing. With the classifier: resistance is predicted at the time of species identification, so the infectious diseases consultation can adjust therapy before phenotypic results are available (Fig. 6).
raw.Stewardship_Details: In eight of the nine cases where the classifier would have changed the empiric regimen the change would have promoted antibiotic stewardship by earlier streamlining to a narrower-spectrum agent; the abstract frames the tool as supporting treatment optimisation and antibiotic stewardship.
raw.Barriers_List: Site-to-site non-transferability (phylogenetic differences, differing resistance prevalence and technical batch effects); performance decay with temporal distance between training and prediction data; many resistance-mediating proteins lie outside the effective mass range of MALDI-TOF MS; sites with small training datasets; absence of a comprehensive catalogue of marker masses; limited representation of high-resistance-burden settings.
raw.Facilitators_List: Existing MALDI-TOF MS infrastructure in clinical laboratories; pre-trained models can expedite uptake; routine clinical acquisition of large-scale MALDI-TOF datasets and combining external datasets improves performance at sites with small datasets; availability of the public DRIAMS database and code.
raw.Future_Directions: Prospective clinical evaluation of the classifier at multiple sites with different prevalence of antimicrobial-resistant bacteria; semi-supervised pre-training on unlabelled MALDI-TOF spectra in DRIAMS before fine-tuning, potentially mitigating batch effects between collection sites via transfer learning; identification of the proteins behind yet-unknown discriminatory feature bins.
raw.Top_Features_Importance_Method: SHAP (Shapley additive explanations) values, plus model feature importance values (LightGBM feature importance and MLP feature importance)
raw.Novel_Predictors_Details: Many highly ranked feature bins have no previously described discriminatory potential; only a subset of peaks (e.g. 2,415 m/z PSM-mec for MRSA, ST131 peaks at 8,448/8,496/11,783 m/z, and proteins at 3,007, 3,891 and 4,511 Da) had been reported before, while the classifiers use the entire spectrum.
raw.Limitation_Categories: Generalisability across sites and over time (batch effects, differing resistance prevalence, phylogenetic variation); mass-range limits of MALDI-TOF MS for resistance-mediating proteins; low-endemic setting; retrospective clinical evaluation only; no prospective or multicentre clinical validation.
raw.Data_Quality_Concerns: Data matching between spectra and resistance profiles had to be developed ad hoc per site and caused substantial data loss (e.g. 40,569 of 186,098 DRIAMS-A spectra lost); resistance labels come from routine laboratory information systems including later-corrected entries, though manual corrections are rare so label uncertainty is limited; hospital-hygiene samples and empty/calibration spectra were excluded.
raw.Reporting_Clarity: Clear: dataset composition, inclusion/exclusion and data loss, splitting strategy, metrics, hyperparameter search and code/data availability are all described.
raw.Page_References: pp. 1-19 (main text pp. 1-11, Methods pp. 12-14, Extended Data pp. 15-19)

raw.Title: Dimensionality reduction and ensemble of LSTMs for antimicrobial resistance prediction
raw.Funder_Names: Spanish Research Agency (grants PID2019-106623RB-C41 and PID2019-107768RA-I00); Community of Madrid / Rey Juan Carlos University Multiannual Agreement, Project Mapping-UCI (Ref F661); IDEAI-UPC Consolidated Research Group Grant from the Catalan Agency of University and Research Grants (AGAUR, Generalitat de Catalunya, 2017 SGR 574); Secretariat for Universities and Research of the Ministry of Research and Universities of the Government of Catalonia and the European Social Fund (2021 FI-B 00965)
raw.Population_Description: Cultures in which the Pseudomonas aeruginosa bacterium was detected in patients admitted to the ICU service of the University Hospital of Fuenlabrada (July 2004 to May 2019): 764 cultures belonging to 277 patients; every instance is a culture of a patient whose ICU stay exceeded 48 h (nosocomial infections).
raw.Top_Predictive_Features: Ranked by the number of antimicrobial families in which each feature is selected (Table 3): antibiotics-ciprofloxacin (5 families), gender (5), reason_admission-acute_respiratory_failure (4), antibiotics-colistin (4), reason_admission-neuromuscular (4), resistance_qui (4), reason_admission-hypovolaemia (4), antibiotics-doxycycline (4), antibiotics-amikacin (4), patient_category-medical_patient (4). The most relevant sets are the patient's admission information, the antibiotics administered, and previous antimicrobial resistance.
raw.Provider_Facing_Applications: Resistance prediction (phenotype from genotype or spectra); Treatment / prescribing guidance
raw.All_Models_Evaluated: Single LSTM network and an ensemble of 20 LSTMs (Horizontal Voting Ensemble), both with the proposed feature selection; test-set AUC averaged over the six antimicrobial families: 67.64% (single network) vs 68.35% (ensemble); validation AUC with FS 70.25% vs 67.55% without FS (all-feature baseline). Three feature-selection methods are also compared: proposed FS, Bootstrap Voting FS and Group Lasso FS.
raw.Best_Performing_Model: Ensemble of 20 LSTMs (Horizontal Voting Ensemble) - highest AUC, statistically significant improvement over a single LSTM on the test sets of all six antimicrobial families
raw.Accuracy_Value: Ensemble of LSTMs, test set (Table 7), no single primary dataset named: 64.25 (AMG), 69.74 (CAR), 45.58 (CF4), 53.02 (PAP), 68.37 (POL), 71.12 (QUI) - highest 71.12% for the QUI family.
raw.Accuracy_Population_Set: Test set of each antimicrobial family (Table 7), ensemble of 20 LSTMs after the proposed feature selection; mean over 50 repetitions.
raw.Sensitivity_Value: Ensemble of LSTMs, test set (Table 7), no single primary dataset named: 59.11 (AMG), 72.58 (CAR), 24.51 (CF4), 28.30 (PAP), 0.0 (POL), 68.65 (QUI) - highest 72.58% for the CAR family.
raw.Sensitivity_Population_Set: Test set of each antimicrobial family (Table 7), ensemble of 20 LSTMs after the proposed feature selection; mean over 50 repetitions.
raw.Specificity_Value: Ensemble of LSTMs, test set (Table 7), no single primary dataset named: 78.21 (AMG), 46.55 (CAR), 83.73 (CF4), 88.09 (PAP), 100.0 (POL), 98.29 (QUI) - highest 100.0% for the POL family, where every instance is classified as susceptible.
raw.Specificity_Population_Set: Test set of each antimicrobial family (Table 7), ensemble of 20 LSTMs after the proposed feature selection; mean over 50 repetitions.
raw.AUROC_Value: Ensemble of LSTMs, test set (Table 7), no single primary dataset named: 76.77 (AMG), 66.53 (CAR), 63.45 (CF4), 71.63 (PAP), 42.32 (POL), 89.37 (QUI) - highest 89.37% for the QUI family.
raw.AUROC_Population_Set: Test set of each antimicrobial family (Table 7), ensemble of 20 LSTMs after the proposed feature selection; mean over 50 repetitions.
raw.Clinical_Maturity_Justification: Data from a single hospital (UHF) split temporally into training (2004-2012), validation and test sets (2013-2019), with patients of the training set discarded from the validation and test sets; no external dataset and no prospective evaluation reported.
raw.Reported_Limitations: The concept drift has not been taken into account because it requires training LSTM networks multiple times, each for a different training window; although the use of windowing could improve network performance, its computational cost is prohibitive.
raw.Unintended_Consequences_Harms: Possible divergence between the predicted antibiogram result and reality in the ICU: there may be a discrepancy between the laboratory antibiogram and what happens in reality, so the LSTM results only reflect how well they predict the antibiogram (gold standard) and physicians must combine the prediction with their medical experience.
raw.Ethical_Governance_Risks: The data comprise confidential patient health information, protected and not releasable without approval by the Committee of Ethics of the University Hospital of Fuenlabrada (Spain).
raw.Reviewer_Notes: 17-page paper, the largest in this wave. Six antimicrobial-family datasets and no single named primary dataset, so the *_Value fields report the ensemble model's per-family test figures with the best family flagged. Judged fields: Provider_Facing_Applications (resistance prediction plus prescribing guidance), Task_Type (multivariate time series classification), the bias/equity fields (answered No on the sentence listing which metrics were computed), Label_Bias_Discussed (Yes: antibiogram gold-standard discrepancy), Novel_Predictors_Identified (Yes: mechanical ventilation and respiratory reasons), Pathogen_Classification left blank because the text never says Gram-negative.
raw.Unresolved_Items: Which antimicrobial family, if any, counts as the primary dataset for the unit-of-analysis *_Value fields; whether the study counts as an AI clinical decision support system (decision-support framing with no implemented CDSS).
raw.Sample_Size: 764 cultures belonging to 277 patients
raw.Conflicts_of_Interest: The authors declare that they have no known competing financial interests or personal relationships that could have appeared to influence the work reported in this paper.
raw.Inclusion_Criteria: Only cultures in which the Pseudomonas aeruginosa bacterium was detected and which belong to patients whose ICU stay is longer than 48 h (nosocomial infections) were considered; instances are modelled as 30-day multivariate time series ending on the day the culture is performed.
raw.Exclusion_Criteria: Instances linked to patients considered in the training set were discarded from the validation and test sets; cultures from patients with an ICU stay of 48 h or less were not considered.
raw.Data_Types_Used: Clinical / EHR variables; Demographic variables; AST phenotypic results; Prescription / dispensing data
raw.Data_Source_Name: Electronic Health Records (EHR) of the ICU service of the University Hospital of Fuenlabrada (UHF)
raw.Dataset_Size: 764 cultures (277 patients); 398 features per time step; 30-day sequences; instances per family: 755 (AMG), 643 (CAR), 749 (CF4), 749 (PAP), 483 (POL), 708 (QUI)
raw.Missing_Data_Method: Unknown values (missing and don't care values) of the don't care subsets of features are encoded as -1, outside the 0-1 normalized range; one indicator feature per subset (admission_indicator, cultures_indicator, icu_admission_indicator) denotes whether the rest of the features of that subset are coded as don't care values.
raw.Geographic_Representativeness: Single Spanish hospital: the ICU service of the University Hospital of Fuenlabrada (Fuenlabrada, Spain); one centre, one country.
raw.Specimen_Type_Detail: culture_type modalities (Annex): abscess, abscess_abdominal, ascitic_fluid, blood, bronchoalveolar_lavage, bronchoaspirate, catheter_vascular, catheter_introductor_, catheter_telescoped, drainage, drainage_abdominal, exudate_axillary, exudate_inguinal, exudate_nasal, exudate_pharynx, exudate_pressure_ulcer_, exudate_rectal, exudate_wound, faeces, liquid_biliary, liquid_peritoneal, liquid_pleural, secretions, sputum, tissue_biopsy, urine
raw.Primary_AMR_Outcome: Binary classification of the antibiogram result (susceptible or resistant) of Pseudomonas aeruginosa cultures for six antibiotic families: Aminoglycosides (AMG), Carbapenems (CAR), 4th Generation Cephalosporins (CF4), Extended-spectrum penicillins (PAP), Polymyxins (POL) and Quinolones (QUI).
raw.Drug_Classes: Aminoglycosides (AMG), Carbapenems (CAR), 4th Generation Cephalosporins (CF4), Extended-spectrum penicillins (PAP), Polymyxins (POL), Quinolones (QUI)
raw.Specific_Antibiotics: Antibiogram panel (Annex, antibiogram_antibiotic modalities), including: amikacin, amoxicillin_clavulanic, ampicillin, ampicillin_sulbactam, aztreonam, cefazolin, cefepime, cefotaxime, cefoxitin, cefpodoxime, ceftazidime, ceftriaxone, cefuroxime, chloramphenicol, ciprofloxacin, clindamycin, colistine, ertapenem, erythromycin, gentamicin, imipenem, levofloxacin, linezolid, meropenem, minocycline, moxifloxacin, nalidixic_acid, nitrofurantoin, norfloxacin, ofloxacin, penicillin_g, phosphomycin, piperacillin, piperacillin_tazobactam, teicoplanin, tetracycline, ticarcilin, tigecycline, tobramycin, trimethoprim_sulfamethoxazole, vancomycin
raw.Resistance_Phenotype_Reported: Binary R/S for a single drug
raw.AMR_Outcome_Definition: Six binary targets, one per antimicrobial family: every target indicates whether the culture's bacterium is susceptible or resistant to the respective antimicrobial family, where a positive is a resistant result and a negative is a susceptible result.
raw.AI_Purpose: To support clinical decisions related to Pseudomonas aeruginosa bacterium by using state-of-the-art Machine Learning techniques to obtain an early prediction of the antibiogram results (susceptible/resistant) from ICU EHR data modelled as multivariate time series and classified with LSTM neural networks.
raw.Num_Models_Compared: 2 classifiers (single LSTM network vs. ensemble of 20 LSTMs); 3 feature-selection methods compared (proposed FS, Bootstrap Voting FS, Group Lasso FS)
raw.Feature_Engineering: In total 398 features, obtained by One-Hot Encoding the categorical variables (a new feature for each category/modality, named feature_name-[modality]); features are organised in three broad groups (temporal features, patient features and ICU features); all features consider information previous to the date and time when the culture is performed.
raw.Feature_Selection_Method: Data-driven wrapper feature selection in two stages: three adapted feature importance techniques (Gradient Feature Importance, Random Subset Feature Importance, Permutation Feature Importance) whose normalized importance values are averaged and sorted, then a Recursive feature number selection algorithm determines the number of features.
raw.Hyperparameter_Method: It was experimentally checked that reducing from 100 to 50 units in both LSTM layers was beneficial when using FS-selected features or the ensemble; the remaining configuration (two stacked LSTM layers with ReLU activation, dropout 0.2, RMSprop, learning rate 10-4 with decay 10-5, 20 epochs extended to 30 for the ensemble) is fixed in Section 3.1.
raw.Software_Libraries: Tensorflow (GradientTape context manager)
raw.Other_Metrics: AUC (area under the ROC curve) is also used to assess performance; values of the loss function (Binary Cross Entropy) are reported; results given as mean and standard deviation over 50 LSTM initializations; statistical significance assessed with a nonparametric test based on bootstrap resampling.
raw.Baseline_Method: LSTM using all 398 features (X, without FS) as baseline; Bootstrap Voting FS and Group Lasso FS as feature-selection comparators
raw.Baseline_Performance: Average AUC among the six families without FS in the validation set 67.55% vs 60.53% in the test set; average AUC with FS: 70.25% in validation and 67.7% in test.
raw.Internal_Validation: Data from 2004 to 2012 were used for the training set and instances from 2013 to 2019 were split into a first half for the validation set and a second half for the test set, with instances linked to patients of the training set discarded from the validation and test sets.
raw.Train_Test_Split: Temporal: instances ordered by culture date, training set 2004-2012, validation and test sets the first and second half of the instances from 2013 to 2019 respectively.
raw.Overfitting_Method: Dropout layers with a rate of 0.2 applied on the LSTM units to mitigate overfitting.
raw.Clinical_Insights: The features identified as most relevant are the antibiotics administered to the patient, the previous antimicrobial resistance and the admission information of the patient; the clinical interpretation is the antibiotic selective pressure phenomenon, and ICU co-admitted-patient features suggest cross-transmission among ICU patients; respiratory-related admission reasons align with the importance of mechanical ventilation.
raw.Generalisability_Details: The small number of instances in the training set (from 284 to 545 training instances depending on the data set) hinders model generalization and causes a high variance in performance.
raw.Maturity_Evidence: Instances are temporally ordered by the date of the culture result and split into training, validation and test sets so that training instances are previous in time to validation instances and validation instances to test instances, with validation applied in all the experiments; training and validation/test patients are disjoint.
raw.Integration_Point: Early prediction of the antibiogram result to support targeted antibiotic therapy decisions for ICU patients, before the result of the susceptibility test (usually 48 h) is available.
raw.End_User_Described: Physicians supporting their decisions in clinical practice (Intensive Care Unit)
raw.Clinical_Workflow_Details: Clinicians carry out a culture to identify the causative bacterium and then a susceptibility test or antibiogram, which guides targeted antibiotic therapy and resistance monitoring in the ICU; the antibiogram usually requires 48 h, so the proposed LSTM provides an early prediction of its result to support the treatment decision.
raw.Barriers_List: High dimensionality of the task; data scarcity (small number of instances); a certain level of class imbalance; concept drift.
raw.Facilitators_List: Clinical collaboration: the proposed methodology and the experimental results have been critically analysed from the clinical point of view with the help of clinicians, and the selected features are meaningful from the clinical perspective because some of them evidence mechanisms of resistance in hospitals.
raw.Future_Directions: Alternative FS algorithms able to deal with multivariate time series (mutual information, Granger causality); class balancing techniques such as undersampling, oversampling or instance weighting, especially for imbalanced families and applied on delimited temporal windows because of concept drift; ensemble learning combining the proposed methods with Logistic Regression and Random Forest; integrating deep neural networks with windowing.
raw.Top_Features_Importance_Method: Importance values are normalized to [0, 1] for each method and then averaged, using Gradient Feature Importance (sensitivity analysis), Random Subset Feature Importance and Permutation Feature Importance; the figure of merit of each method is the average among Accuracy, Sensitivity and Specificity.
raw.Novel_Predictors_Details: Mechanical ventilation and respiratory-related admission reasons remain relevant, suggesting an increased probability of acquiring resistance as a consequence of using mechanical ventilation during the ICU stay; features of co-admitted ICU patients point to cross-transmission among ICU patients.
raw.Limitation_Categories: High dimensionality; data scarcity (small number of instances); class imbalance; concept drift.
raw.Data_Quality_Concerns: A high number of unknown values, comprising both missing values and don't care values; missing values are found in resistance-[modality] and icu_resistance-[modality] features and are encoded with -1 when the antimicrobial family has not been tested; Table 1 reports the percentage of days with unknown values for each feature or set of features.
raw.Reporting_Clarity: Clear: an Annex lists all the features considered in the study with all their different modalities, and the description of each feature meaning is provided in the methods section.
raw.Page_References: pp. 1-17; data pp. 2-4, methods pp. 5-9, results pp. 9-14, discussion pp. 13-15, Annex and references pp. 15-17

AUROC value taken from the training set (primary dataset); the internal-validation C-statistic 0.828 is recorded in All_Models_Evaluated. The paper reports no accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, PPV or F1.

raw.Conflicts_of_Interest: The authors declare no conflict of interest.

Metrics belong to the combined training cohort (n = 261) and the external combined testing cohort (n = 81).

Both are recorded here; testing-cohort AUC/F1 come from the text, the rest from Table 2.
raw.Sample_Size: 454 patients with proven active TB in total; combined cohort (both signs) n = 261 training and n = 81 testing; TIB sign n = 295 training / 102 testing; nodules n = 302 training / 97 testing
raw.Conflicts_of_Interest: The authors declare no relationships with any companies whose products or services may be related to the subject matter of the article.
raw.Sex_Distribution: Combined training cohort: 78 male and 72 female DS-TB patients, 59 male and 52 female MDR-TB patients. Combined testing cohort: 26 male and 19 female DS-TB patients, 23 male and 13 female MDR-TB patients (counts, Table 1; no percentages stated).
raw.Inclusion_Criteria: Culture, sputum microscopy or PCR confirmation of TB; drug susceptibility test (DST) results for M. tuberculosis to distinguish DS-TB from MDR-TB; typical imaging findings (TIB sign or nodules) indicative of TB; all CT scans performed before the TB diagnosis.
raw.Exclusion_Criteria: Image artifacts or incomplete clinical information; a history of other pulmonary diseases such as lung cancer or COPD; diabetes or HIV seropositivity.
raw.Data_Types_Used: Imaging; AST phenotypic results; Demographic variables
raw.Data_Source_Name: No named database - chest CT data and DST results collected retrospectively from two hospitals (hospital 1 and hospital 2)
raw.Dataset_Size: 454 patients; cohorts TIB n = 295 training / 102 testing, nodules n = 302 / 97, combined n = 261 / 81; 1483 radiomics features extracted per sign
raw.Geographic_Representativeness: Two Chinese hospitals (hospital 1 and an unnamed hospital 2) in Beijing; cohorts are single-city and the paper does not discuss how far they represent the wider TB population.
raw.Specimen_Type_Detail: Chest CT images (lung windows) of the TIB sign and nodules; TB confirmation by culture, sputum microscopy or PCR
raw.Primary_AMR_Outcome: Multidrug-resistant TB (MDR-TB) versus drug-sensitive TB (DS-TB) among patients with active tuberculosis: MDR-TB is resistance to isoniazid and rifampicin, established by drug susceptibility testing, and predicted from CT radiomics features.
raw.Drug_Classes: First-line anti-tuberculosis drugs (isoniazid, rifampicin)
raw.Specific_Antibiotics: Isoniazid; rifampicin
raw.AMR_Outcome_Definition: Binary MDR vs DS label: MDR-TB is resistance to isoniazid and rifampicin; patients were classified from drug susceptibility test (DST) results for M. tuberculosis, and the radiomics models predict this MDR-TB/DS-TB status.
raw.AI_Purpose: To develop and validate CT radiomics machine-learning models based on the tree-in-bud sign and nodules (and their combination) that predict multidrug-resistant TB in active TB patients, as a non-invasive alternative to microbiologic culture and DST.
raw.Num_Models_Compared: 3 (TIB model, nodules model, combined model)
raw.Feature_Engineering: Manual ROI segmentation of the TIB sign and nodules in 3D Slicer; radiomics features extracted with PyRadiomics (preprocessing per Supplementary Material); 1483 features per sign, comprising first-order, shape-based (3D, 2D), GLCM, GLRLM, GLSZM, GLDM and NGTDM features.
raw.Feature_Selection_Method: Intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC > 0.80) on a 30-patient resegmentation subset to retain reproducible features; maximal information coefficient (MIC) to retain the top 200 features per sign; recursive feature elimination (RFE) with tenfold cross-validation to select the final 16 (TIB) and 15 (nodules) features.
raw.Num_Features_Total: 1483 radiomics features extracted separately for the TIB sign and for nodules
raw.Num_Features_Selected: 16 features from the TIB sign and 15 from nodules (31 in the combined model)
raw.Class_Imbalance_Method: Synthetic minority oversampling technique (SMOTE) applied to the training cohort to handle imbalance between DS-TB and MDR-TB patients
raw.Software_Libraries: Python Scikit-learn package (Scikit-learn Version 0.21); SPSS version 26 for statistical analysis
raw.Other_Metrics: DeLong test p-values comparing AUCs between the three models; decision curve analysis (DCA) net benefit across threshold probabilities; feature ICC for reproducibility.
raw.Baseline_Method: DeLong test comparing the AUCs of the TIB, nodule and combined models; decision curve analysis against the treat-all and treat-none strategies.
raw.Baseline_Performance: All three models offered net benefits over the treat-all or treat-none schemes within a certain range of thresholds in the combined training cohort, with similar results in the testing cohort; the DeLong test showed no significant AUC difference between the combined and nodules models (training p = 0.538).
raw.Internal_Validation: Each training cohort randomly divided into parts at a ratio of 7:3 using tenfold cross-validation; feature reproducibility checked by ICC on a 30-patient resegmentation subset.
raw.Train_Test_Split: Random 7:3 split of each training cohort (with tenfold cross-validation); the three external testing cohorts from hospital 2 served as independent test sets.
raw.External_Validation_Description: Testing cohorts from hospital 2: 102 patients with the TIB sign, 97 with nodules and 81 with both signs (enrolled August 2017 to March 2022), separate from the hospital 1 training cohorts (December 2015 to January 2022).
raw.Overfitting_Method: Tenfold cross-validation used to avoid overfitting; DeLong test used to evaluate whether overfitting occurred.
raw.Clinical_Insights: The paper argues the TIB sign reflects endobronchial spread, caseous necrosis and granulomatous inflammation, but that imaging signs alone cannot separate MDR-TB from DS-TB, so quantitative radiomics is needed; the models (especially the combined and nodule models) are presented as supporting early, non-invasive identification of MDR before TB progression.
raw.Generalisability_Details: The models were applied in the combined cohorts to guarantee stability and generalizability in clinical practice, and the limitations note that future prospective studies are needed to increase generalizability given the small testing cohort.
raw.Maturity_Evidence: Best model of all models selected and tested on the corresponding cohort of three external testing cohorts (hospital 2); internal 7:3 split with tenfold cross-validation. No prospective evaluation, no integration into clinical systems and no routine use reported.
raw.Integration_Point: Chest CT interpretation / radiology workflow, proposed as a non-invasive auxiliary diagnostic tool in routine clinical practice.
raw.End_User_Described: Not explicitly named; the paper proposes use as a diagnostic tool in routine clinical practice, i.e. the clinician interpreting chest CT (radiologist / chest physician) is the implied end user.
raw.Barriers_List: Retrospective design and small sample size with potential selection bias; models apply only to patients showing the TIB sign or nodules; limited clinical information and no clinical variables included; small testing cohort limiting generalizability.
raw.Facilitators_List: Non-invasive imaging-based prediction of MDR-TB; user-friendly, before culture/DST results become available (4-8 weeks); net benefit over treat-all/treat-none strategies; complementary information from the TIB sign and nodules.
raw.Future_Directions: Prospective studies with larger testing cohorts to increase generalizability, and investigation of radiomics in TB patients without the TIB sign or nodules.
raw.Top_Features_Importance_Method: Normalised importance, presented in Fig. 3 (no named importance or permutation method in the text)
raw.Limitation_Categories: Retrospective single-period design; small sample size; selection bias; restricted to patients with the TIB sign or nodules; limited clinical information / no clinical predictors in the models; small testing cohort and need for prospective studies.
raw.Data_Quality_Concerns: Cases with image artifacts or incomplete clinical information were excluded; feature reproducibility assessed by ICC (> 0.80 retained) on a 30-patient resegmentation subset; ROIs drawn manually layer by layer and confirmed by a second radiologist blinded to DST results.
raw.Reporting_Clarity: Design, cohorts, feature selection (ICC, MIC, RFE), classifier, validation strategy and the three models' metrics are reported clearly, with AUC 95% CIs and Table 2 covering all three models; the individual radiomics features are shown only in figures, and the DST method and breakpoints used for the MDR/DS label are not specified.

raw.Unintended_Consequences_Harms: None reported; the authors caution that the rapid screening assay cannot replace conventional molecular methods for detecting CRKP, CPKP and colistin resistance.
raw.Ethical_Governance_Risks: No ethical or governance risks are discussed; the study reports IRB approval (CMUH109-REC3-098 and CMUH112-REC2-027) and waiver of informed consent.
raw.Reviewer_Notes: Unit of analysis = LightGBM on the primary CRKP/CSKP task (accuracy 0.8869, AUC 0.9551, F1 0.8703); the colistin model's figures (0.8361/0.8447/0.8925) are recorded in All_Models_Evaluated. Sensitivity, specificity, PPV, NPV, confidence intervals, calibration and any baseline comparison are not reported. The same LightGBM model produces all outputs, so there is a single model and no model-vs-model comparison.
raw.Unresolved_Items: Age, sex, and ethnicity of the 34 evaluated patients are not reported; specimen types used for the clinical evaluation are listed but not the per-specimen case counts beyond the aggregate.
raw.Sample_Size: 830 CRKP isolates (plus 1462 CSKP and 227 CRKP from NTUH used for modelling and 419 CRKP from CMUH for validation); 54 ColRKP and 1592 ColIKP isolates; 34 patients in the clinical evaluation. Unit = isolates (and patients for the clinical evaluation).
raw.Conflicts_of_Interest: None declared.
raw.Inclusion_Criteria: Clinical specimens included patients with blood specimens, endotracheal aspirates, bronchoalveolar lavage, body fluid from sterile sites, and catheter tip cultures; the isolate collections comprised K. pneumoniae isolates from the SMART programme, NTUH and CMUH.
raw.Exclusion_Criteria: Isolates with multiple carbapenemases were ruled out of the ML modelling because the MALDI-TOF target analyte is protein; the NG-Test CARBA 5 result was used first for follow-up ML.
raw.Data_Types_Used: MALDI-TOF mass spectra; AST phenotypic results; Gene presence / AMR genotype; Clinical / EHR variables
raw.Data_Source_Name: SMART (Surveillance of Multicenter Antimicrobial Resistance in Taiwan) programme of the Taiwan Centers for Disease Control; National Taiwan University Hospital (NTUH); China Medical University Hospital (CMUH)
raw.Dataset_Size: SMART/NTUH modelling set: 1462 CSKP and 227 CRKP isolates from NTUH plus 184 blood CRKP isolates from SMART; validation set: 419 CRKP isolates from CMUH; colistin set: 54 ColRKP and 1592 ColIKP isolates.
raw.Geographic_Representativeness: Isolates came from a single country (Taiwan) and the authors state the discoveries were based on isolates collected in a local part of Taiwan, requiring larger external validation.
raw.Specimen_Type_Detail: blood specimens, endotracheal aspirates, bronchoalveolar lavage, body fluid from sterile sites, and catheter tip cultures
raw.Primary_AMR_Outcome: Carbapenem resistance (CRKP vs CSKP), carbapenemase Ambler class (A/KPC, B/NDM-VIM-IMP, D/OXA-48), and colistin resistance (ColRKP vs ColIKP) predicted directly from routine MALDI-TOF MS spectra
raw.Pathogens: Klebsiella pneumoniae (carbapenem-resistant CRKP, carbapenem-susceptible CSKP, carbapenemase-producing CPKP, colistin-resistant ColRKP and colistin-intermediate ColIKP isolates)
raw.Drug_Classes: Carbapenems (ertapenem, imipenem, meropenem); polymyxins (colistin)
raw.Specific_Antibiotics: ertapenem, imipenem, meropenem (carbapenem non-susceptibility definition); colistin (resistance criterion >=4 mg/L)
raw.Resistance_Phenotype_Reported: Binary R/S for a single drug; CRE / carbapenemase-producing
raw.AMR_Outcome_Definition: CRKP = non-susceptible (intermediate and resistant) to at least one carbapenem antibiotic with an MIC value of >=1, >=2, and >=2 mg/L for ertapenem, imipenem, and meropenem respectively, according to CLSI guidelines; colistin resistance criterion >=4 mg/L by broth microdilution.
raw.AI_Purpose: To build an ML model that predicts CRKP, carbapenemase-producing K. pneumoniae and colistin resistance directly from routine MALDI-TOF MS spectra, and to analyse retrospectively the clinical implications of reporting the predictions to physicians before the final report.
raw.Feature_Engineering: Spectra resampled to a fixed sampling rate (1 Da); TopHat baseline correction, square root transformation and Savitzky-Golay filter for baseline correction, normalization and smoothing; min-max scaling to 0-1; spectra extracted from m/z 2000-20000 Da and grouped into 10 Dalton bins, taking the maximum peak intensity per bin.
raw.Feature_Selection_Method: SHAP (SHapely Additive exPlanation) values used to rank features; the top 10 most important features were identified.
raw.Num_Features_Total: Not stated as a count; spectra extracted over m/z 2000 to 20000 Da and grouped into 10 Dalton bins (one bin = one attribute)
raw.Num_Features_Selected: 10 (top 10 most important features identified by SHAP)
raw.Class_Imbalance_Method: The five carbapenemase genes (KPC, OXA, NDM, VIM, IMP) were regrouped into three Ambler classes - A (KPC), B (NDM, VIM, IMP) and D (OXA) - because the extreme imbalance across categories reduced the robustness and generality of the model.
raw.Software_Libraries: LightGBM; TopHat; Savitzky-Golay filter (Python version 3.7)
raw.Other_Metrics: None beyond accuracy, area under the curve (AUC) and F1 score for the models; the clinical evaluation reported the time saved, proportion of CRKP in the final culture, proportion of antibiotic regimen adjustments and hospital mortality rate.
raw.Internal_Validation: five-fold train-test split for training and validation
raw.Train_Test_Split: Five-fold train-test split (split proportions not stated)
raw.External_Validation_Description: 419 CRKP isolates collected randomly from the China Medical University Hospital (CMUH) between 2019 and 2022 formed the validation set, separate from the SMART/NTUH isolates used for modelling.
raw.Overfitting_Method: Regrouping the imbalanced carbapenemase classes into three Ambler classes and using a five-fold train-test split for training and validation.
raw.Clinical_Insights: The top-ranking protein marker m/z 4520-4529 distinguishes KPC from OXA, NDM, IMP and VIM among CRKP isolates; SHAP-ranked m/z 4170-4179 separates ColRKP from ColIKP.
raw.Generalisability_Details: The authors note the isolates came from a local part of Taiwan and that other isolates with different sequence types (the main sequence type was ST11) should be included for validation in further research.
raw.Maturity_Evidence: Evidence of external validation: the remaining 419 CRKP isolates for validation were collected randomly from CMUH between 2019 and 2022, separate from the SMART/NTUH modelling isolates; the model was also run prospectively on routine isolates for preliminary reporting between February 25 and May 15, 2022.
raw.Integration_Point: Preliminary reporting of the MALDI-TOF MS-based ML CRKP prediction (result and probability) to the clinicians responsible for patient care before the final culture report, conveyed by texting.
raw.End_User_Described: Clinicians responsible for patient care (physicians) receiving preliminary CRKP prediction results
raw.Clinical_Workflow_Details: After modelling and validation the model operates within the routine clinical workflow: the MALDI-TOF MS results are used directly for prediction without any additional experimental procedures.
raw.Stewardship_Details: Of patients with CRKP infection, 79.2% (19/24) received inappropriate empirical antibiotics and the antibiotic regimen was changed in 73.7% (14/19) of cases after the preliminary ML prediction results.
raw.Barriers_List: Isolates from a local part of Taiwan requiring larger external validation; MALDI-TOF MS results from a single isolate not sufficiently representative for phenotype prediction; identity and resistance role of the important features not established.
raw.Facilitators_List: MALDI-TOF MS is a more suitable data source than genomic or genetic data for ML-based AMR prediction because it is obtained from routine clinical diagnostic workflows and the predictions can be applied clinically.
raw.Future_Directions: Other isolates with different sequence types should be included for validation in further research; larger external validation is needed; further biomarkers or functional segment experiments are needed to reveal the identity of each important feature and its role in drug resistance mechanisms.
raw.Top_Features_Importance_Method: SHAP (SHapely Additive exPlanation) values
raw.Novel_Predictors_Details: The top-ranking protein marker m/z 4520-4529 could differentiate KPC from OXA, NDM, IMP and VIM carbapenemases among CRKP isolates, providing additional information beyond previous reports that compared mainly KPC2-positive and KPC2-negative isolates.
raw.Feature_Interactions_Method: SHAP values, which consider the interactions between features and their effect on the model's predictions
raw.Limitation_Categories: Geography/generalisability (single local region of Taiwan, need for larger external validation); data representativeness (single-isolate MALDI-TOF spectra); unexplained features (identity and resistance role of important features unknown); the assay cannot replace conventional molecular methods.
raw.Data_Quality_Concerns: MALDI-TOF MS results from one isolate were not sufficiently representative of the input data for drug-resistant phenotype prediction given variation among samples; further biomarkers or functional experiments are needed to reveal the identity of each important feature.
raw.Reporting_Clarity: The model, metrics and clinical evaluation are reported explicitly and the MALDI-TOF MS data were deposited in Zenodo; however no reporting guideline is named and no code is shared.

raw.Title: Development and validation of a prediction model for unsuccessful treatment outcomes in patients with multi-drug resistance tuberculosis
raw.Funder_Names: Social Development Project, Science and Technology Department of Shaanxi Province (2016SF-032); Medical Research Project of Science and Technology in Xi'an (21YXYJ0001, 21YXYJ0075)
raw.Population_Description: 446 patients diagnosed with multi-drug resistant pulmonary tuberculosis (MDR-PTB) at a single special hospital in Xi'an, China, treated Jan 2017 - Dec 2019 and followed to treatment outcome
raw.Age_Mean_Median: 38.1 ± 15.0 years (reported as median age, mean ± SD)
raw.Top_Predictive_Features: 1) No health education; 2) advanced age; 3) male sex; 4) larger extent of lung involvement (lung lesion fields). Selected by LASSO regression (optimal lambda 0.062) then multivariable logistic regression; adjusted ORs 0.44 for health education, 2.43 for male sex, 1.04 per year of age, 1.25 per extra lung lesion field
raw.Provider_Facing_Applications: Screening / risk stratification
raw.All_Models_Evaluated: Only one model was developed and evaluated: the multivariable logistic-regression nomogram - AUC 0.757 (95%CI 0.711 to 0.804), C-index 0.75, bootstrap-corrected C-index 0.747, leave-one-out cross-validation C-index 0.765, sensitivity 0.640, specificity 0.773, calibration slope 0.968. Models from other studies are cited but not re-evaluated: Brazil 802-patient model (AUC 0.76) and a Hunan model with moderate AUC
raw.Sensitivity_Population_Set: Training cohort (446 patients)
raw.Specificity_Population_Set: Training cohort (446 patients)
raw.AUROC_Population_Set: Training cohort (446 patients)
raw.Clinical_Maturity_Justification: Internal validation only - bootstrap sampling (1000 resamples, corrected C-index 0.747) and leave-one-out cross-validation (C-index 0.765); the model was not externally validated
raw.Reported_Limitations: Observational study so confounding cannot be completely excluded and causality is not proven; conducted in one hospital with no external validation, a regional limitation; newer drugs (bedaquiline, delamanid) were not used so the model does not apply to newer regimens; HIV co-infection not analysed (only two HIV-positive cases) so the model cannot be used in HIV-positive patients; Mpb64 monoclonal antibody is not a recommended method of Mtb identification; systematic health education not yet widely conducted
raw.Sample_Size: 446 patients
raw.Conflicts_of_Interest: The authors have no conflicts of interest to declare.
raw.Inclusion_Criteria: Patients diagnosed with MDR-PTB at Xi'an Chest Hospital between Jan 2017 and Dec 2019, treated with the 2016 drug-resistant TB treatment guidelines regimen for 18 to 24 months
raw.Exclusion_Criteria: Patients who died before the start of MDR-TB treatment, received an incorrect regimen (lack enough core medication), were co-infected with non-tuberculosis mycobacterium, or received a short-term regimen
raw.Data_Types_Used: Clinical / EHR variables; Demographic variables; AST phenotypic results; Imaging
raw.Data_Source_Name: Xi'an Chest Hospital electronic medical record system (no named dataset; managed in EpiData)
raw.Dataset_Size: 543 patients diagnosed; 446 included in the analysis (299 successful, 147 unsuccessful)
raw.Missing_Data_Method: 24 cases missing fluoroquinolone and injectable-agent drug sensitivity tests were inserted ('imputed') according to the resistance rate; older cases with longer use of these drugs were inserted as resistant
raw.Geographic_Representativeness: Single hospital in Xi'an, Shaanxi Province, China; the authors compare their patient characteristics with a national survey in China, Japan and the 2020 Global TB Report and argue the model may apply to other regions
raw.Specimen_Type_Detail: sputum/BALF smear
raw.Primary_AMR_Outcome: Unsuccessful MDR-PTB treatment outcome (treatment failure, loss to follow-up, or death) versus treatment success (cure or treatment completion), reclassified from the six WHO treatment outcome categories
raw.Drug_Classes: Anti-tuberculosis drugs: fluoroquinolones, injectable agents, linezolid, cycloserine, clofazimine, ethambutol, pyrazinamide, prothionamide, P-aminosalicylate
raw.Specific_Antibiotics: Isoniazid, rifampin, levofloxacin, moxifloxacin, amikacin, capreomycin (DST panel); bedaquiline, delamanid, linezolid, clofazimine, cycloserine, ethambutol, pyrazinamide, prothionamide, P-aminosalicylate (drugs in regimens)
raw.Resistance_Phenotype_Reported: MDR; Binary R/S for a single drug
raw.AMR_Outcome_Definition: MDR-TB defined as M. tuberculosis resistance to isoniazid and rifampicin; drug sensitivity coded sensitive/resistant for fluoroquinolones and injectable agents by BACTEC MGIT 960 and absolute concentration methods; outcome label = unsuccessful treatment outcome
raw.AI_Purpose: To develop and validate a simple clinical prediction model (nomogram) to predict unsuccessful treatment outcomes in patients with multi-drug resistant pulmonary tuberculosis
raw.Num_Models_Compared: 1 (a single multivariable logistic-regression nomogram; no head-to-head model comparison)
raw.Feature_Engineering: Lung lesion distribution derived from post-anterior chest radiographs divided into six fields (lines at the lower edge of the second and fourth ribs), counting lesion-bearing fields rather than lesion area; age and health-education status used as recorded
raw.Feature_Selection_Method: LASSO regression for selection, then multivariable logistic regression
raw.Hyperparameter_Method: Optimal lambda (0.062) selected in LASSO regression via the partial likelihood deviance profile
raw.Software_Libraries: Free Statistics software version 1.5 used alongside R version 3.3.2; no R packages named
raw.Other_Metrics: AUC 0.757 (95%CI 0.711 to 0.804); C-index 0.75; bootstrap-corrected C-index 0.747; leave-one-out cross-validation C-index 0.765 and calibration slope 1.0; calibration slope 0.968 with bootstrap sampling; Youden index 0.382; decision curve analysis net benefit at threshold probabilities 0.086-0.713
raw.Internal_Validation: 1000 bootstrap sampling for corrected ROC, C-index and calibration curve; leave-one-out cross-validation
raw.Train_Test_Split: No separate train/test split reported; the full 446-patient cohort was used with internal validation (bootstrap sampling and leave-one-out cross-validation)
raw.CV_Folds: Leave-one-out cross-validation (one held-out patient per fold); no k-fold scheme reported
raw.Overfitting_Method: LASSO shrinkage used for variable selection and bootstrap-corrected C-index (0.747) reported; overfitting not discussed explicitly
raw.Clinical_Insights: Each prognostc factor carries fixed nomogram points (age 60 years = 65 points, male = 25, 4 lung lesion fields = 18, no health education = 24), so a 60-year-old man with 4 lung lesion fields and no health education totals 132 points, about a 70% risk of unsuccessful outcome; a one-year increase in age raises incidence by 4% and each extra lung lesion field by 25%
raw.Generalisability_Details: Authors argue their prognostic model may apply to patients in other regions of China on the basis of comparable patient characteristics, but state it was not externally validated, does not apply to newer regimens and is most useful in settings such as west China where newer drugs are unavailable
raw.Maturity_Evidence: Internal validation evidence only: 1000-sample bootstrap correction (C-index 0.747) and leave-one-out cross-validation (C-index 0.765); the paper states the model was not externally validated
raw.Integration_Point: At the start of MDR-TB treatment, from baseline characteristics collected on admission, to identify patients at risk of an unsuccessful outcome
raw.End_User_Described: Clinicians treating patients with MDR-PTB
raw.Barriers_List: Newer drugs (bedaquiline, delamanid) were not used in this cohort and are not always available, especially in west China, so the model does not apply to newer regimens; systematic health education is not yet widely conducted; the model cannot be used in HIV-positive patients
raw.Facilitators_List: All four factors are baseline characteristics that can be acquired easily; model showed good discrimination and calibration and was validated by bootstrap and leave-one-out cross-validation; systematic health education programme supported by FHI 360
raw.Future_Directions: Wider implementation of systematic health education and further use of the nomogram to improve MDR-TB treatment outcomes
raw.Top_Features_Importance_Method: Multivariable logistic regression adjusted odds ratios with 95% CIs, LASSO regression selection and nomogram point scores
raw.Limitation_Categories: Confounding / no causality (observational); single hospital and no external validation (regional limitation); treatment era / newer regimens (bedaquiline, delamanid not used); exclusion of HIV-positive patients; diagnostic method (Mpb64 monoclonal antibody not recommended); limited implementation of systematic health education
raw.Data_Quality_Concerns: Data managed in EpiData and entered by individuals, with entered data and outcomes checked by attending doctors; 24 missing DST values inserted by imputation based on resistance rate
raw.Reporting_Clarity: Clear reporting of design, participants, prognostic factors and model performance (AUC, C-index, calibration); no statement of adherence to any reporting guideline
